pr_body:
One of the ManagementObjectTests retries with ERROR_NOT_READY or occasionally ERROR_INVALID_BLOCK or ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY. Adding additional retries won't improve the situation, so we disable the test on the only platform it's failing on, which is Windows 11.

Updates #70414

review_comments: What is the instability?  Normally we disable tests on some OS and earlier due to issues in the OS later fixed, but this is disabling it for all future versions.  Is there an issue in the implementation of ManagementClass then we need to address?  A known bug in the OS that we're waiting for a fix on and need to re-enable the test starting from a certain OS version? Etc.

There are a couple of these in System.Diagnostics.EventLog (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58829). Our assumption is an OS bug as our code didn't change. 

I think disabling for Windows 11 makes sense in this situation. However we should probably leave the issue open (remove "Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/70414" from description above). Ideally we'd also disable in such a way that it re-enables itself on Windows "12" but  what would that be -- 23000?
Ideally we'd also open bugs against the OS, but for flaky issues like this that's pretty expensive and given it's a legacy API it might not be a high priority.

> Ideally we'd also disable in such a way that it re-enables itself on Windows "12" but what would that be -- 23000?

I noticed the dev channel releases use 25000+ in their build numbers. Is it safe to assume 23000 is reserved for Windows 12?
